author.heading: About the Nixon screenplay writers
author.metaLine: Stephen J. Rivele, Christopher Wilkinson and Oliver Stone · Nixon (1995)
author.bio: Oliver Stone directed Nixon and shares its screenplay credit with Stephen J. Rivele and Christopher Wilkinson. Their Mao–Nixon scene is dramatic writing, so dialogue assigned to Mao in the film must not be quoted as if it were a historical meeting transcript.

misattribution.heading: Often misattributed
misattribution.intro: The actor’s character is a representation of Mao, not the author of the screenplay.

items.why: Wikiquote ↗ traces the alleged saying to a fictionalized film scene.

misattribution.truthLine: Credit the jointly written screenplay, and retain the distinction between “in us” and the popular “within us” variant.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The film stages a conversation in which Mao and Nixon reflect on the human drives behind political conflict. Because the character bears a historical leader’s name, removing the movie context turns a screenwriter’s line into what looks like documentary testimony.

schema.claimReviewed: The historical Mao Zedong said “The real war is within us. History is a symptom of our disease.”
schema.faqAnswer: No. This is dialogue from Nixon (1995), co-written by Oliver Stone, Stephen J. Rivele and Christopher Wilkinson, not a documented saying of the historical Mao. The fetched transcription also reads “in us,” not “within us.”
schema.verdictNote: The screenplay is jointly credited to Stephen J. Rivele, Christopher Wilkinson and Oliver Stone. “Nixon screenplay writers” names that three-person writing team, not one writer or the historical Mao.
